name: Auth Foundation
purpose: Coordinate one complete in-process Auth Service product candidate through the CAV2-D65 revision-2 prototype chain while keeping trusted-input resolution, authorization-state resolution, generated decision logic, service composition, product tests, product approval, and later operational authority in distinct evidence and decision lanes.
scope: one complete in-process Auth Service that resolves trusted request inputs and authorization state from SQLite, constructs a trusted command, evaluates exact session-role-permission state, and returns only ALLOW or DENY

one CAV2-D65 revision-2 prototype chain from definition prototypes and agent-facing ontology scaffolds through product, business-ontology, DomainSpec, compiled-system, implementation, frozen candidate, current product tests, and product approval
one EVF seven-seam campaign as a sibling product-test branch for the exact frozen Auth Service candidate
deterministic compiled artifacts, generated Rust correspondence, fail-closed behavior, and immutable candidate-bound evidence
exclusions: token creation, validation, refresh, or revocation transport
administrative mutation APIs, audit transport, multi-node operation, deployment, and production-security claims

treating this Project, Goal, plan DAG, ontology view, prototype binding, or validator output as implementation, product approval, admission, activation, publication, release, deployment, or external-effect authority

evidence_index.supports: The D65 revision-2 DAG fixes the bounded Auth Service product, construction stages, evidence join, layering, Smallest Working Units, and stop before post-approval authority.
evidence_index.claim_limit: The DAG is planning evidence only. It does not admit a Design, authorize implementation, prove any stage complete, approve the product, or authorize an external effect.

challenge_route: Challenge Project scope through the Auth Foundation Project owner, product meaning through the CyberAlchemy v2 product owner, DomainSpec construction claims through the DomainSpec v2 owner, implementation claims through the Auth Service implementation owner, product-test claims through the Auth Service product-test owner, product approval through the Auth Service product owner, and every later authority effect through its separately selected owner.
